items.title: Securitization cash waterfall
items.direction_label: Cash pours in at the top and falls tier by tier: each class is paid only after the one above it

steps.text: Collateral cash flows come in from the asset pool
steps.detail: A waterfall details how collateral cash flows are distributed to the classes of bondholders.

steps.text: Fees and defaults are taken off
steps.detail: Fees and defaults reduce the net cash available before any tranche is paid.
Senior sits at the top of the capital structure: highest priority for principal and interest, lowest coupon.

steps.text: Mezzanine claims are paid, if senior is paid in full
steps.detail: Mezzanine is junior to senior and absorbs losses after the equity tranche.
Equity has the lowest priority and a variable return: whatever is left.

steps.text: Excess above the OC trigger goes to the trust account
steps.detail: If cash flows to equity exceed the overcollateralization trigger, the excess is diverted to a trust account.

items.explanation: The notes draw the three-tier waterfall as a single ordered chain with an "order of payment" arrow: fees and defaults come off first, senior is paid first, mezzanine only if senior is paid in full, equity takes the residual, and excess above the OC trigger is diverted to the trust account. Losses run the opposite way: equity absorbs the first losses, then mezzanine.
